metadata.case_name: SO CHO YIN v. MTR CORPORATION LTD

injuries.description: Local tenderness at the left parietal area of her head
source: She was found to have local tenderness at the left parietal area of her head, nasal bridge, back, buttock and the right ankle.
injuries.icd_description: Contusion of other or unspecified sites of head

source: She was found to have local tenderness at the left parietal area of her head, nasal bridge, back, buttock and the right ankle.

injuries.description: Residual pain in the low back and buttock
source: This consisted of 5% for residual pain in the low back and buttock; 1% for the residual pain in the ankle and hand; and 2% for residual pain in the neck due to possible sprain injury.
injuries.icd_description: Strain or sprain of muscle, fascia or tendon of lower back

injuries.description: Decrease in sensation and power diffusely over the left side of the body
source: There was decrease in sensation and power diffusely over the left side of the body.

injuries.description: Mild tenderness over the mid-dorsal aspect of the left wrist; pain in the left wrist
source: During her subsequent visits to the hospital, So complained about decrease in sensation over the left side of her body and pain in the left wrist, neck and right ankle. Regarding the left wrist, examination revealed mild tenderness over the mid-dorsal aspect but no associated external wound, bruising, deformity or ligamental laxity.
injuries.icd_description: Superficial injury of other parts of wrist or hand, unspecified

injuries.description: Tenderness over the right ankle (some tenderness over both medial and lateral region)
source: She was found to have local tenderness at the left parietal area of her head, nasal bridge, back, buttock and the right ankle.
Regarding the ankle, there was some tenderness over both medial and lateral region, yet the motion range was good.
injuries.icd_description: Superficial injury of ankle or foot

injuries.description: Pain in the neck due to possible sprain injury; percussion tenderness at the cervical thorax junction with decreased neck and trunk movement range
source: Examination of the neck revealed percussion tenderness at the cervical thorax junction, thoracolumbar junction and lumbosacral junction with decreased neck and trunk movement range.
This consisted of 5% for residual pain in the low back and buttock; 1% for the residual pain in the ankle and hand; and 2% for residual pain in the neck due to possible sprain injury.
injuries.icd_description: Acute whiplash associated disorder with complaint of neck pain with musculoskeletal signs

manifestations.description: Local tenderness at the left parietal area of her head
Residual pain in the low back and buttock
Decrease in sensation over the left side of the body
Weakness over left side of body (diffuse weakness)
Mild tenderness over the mid-dorsal aspect of the left wrist
Tenderness over the right ankle with good range of motion
Decreased neck and trunk movement range; percussion tenderness at the cervical thorax junction
